ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a common-emitter amplifier circuit. The input signal is applied through coupling capacitor C1 to the base of transistor VT, and Rb1 and Rb2 form the base-bias voltage divider. The collector is connected through resistor Rc to +Vcc, the emitter has Re, and is bypassed by Ce. The collector output node is connected through coupling capacitor C2 to the output terminal on the right side, and load resistor RL is connected from the output terminal to the lower common ground line. Reasoning: Under normal mid-frequency amplification conditions, coupling capacitor C2 is approximately a short circuit for AC signals, so RL is equivalently connected at the collector AC output terminal, and for AC gain it forms a parallel load with Rc. The magnitude of the common-emitter voltage gain is approximately proportional to Rc || RL. When the load is normally connected, the equivalent collector load is Rc || RL; if RL is open-circuit, then RL is equivalent to infinity, Rc || ∞ = Rc. Because Rc is greater than Rc || RL, after open-circuit the equivalent load resistance increases, and the voltage gain magnitude increases.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the image as a voltage-divider biased BJT common-emitter amplifier: input is coupled through C1 to the base, Rc connects the collector to +VCC, Re is bypassed by Ce, and the output is coupled from the collector through C2 to the load resistor RL on the right.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Under midband/normal amplification, C1, C2, and Ce are treated as AC shorts, +VCC is AC ground, and the common-emitter voltage gain magnitude is approximately proportional to the collector AC load: |Av| ≈ gm(Rc || RL), or equivalently β(Rc || RL)/rbe when the emitter is bypassed. method.method_draft: Treat the circuit as a common-emitter amplifier driving an external load through C2. In the normal loaded state, RL draws signal current and lowers the effective output resistance seen at the collector, reducing the output voltage for a given input. If RL is opened, the load current becomes zero and the collector/output is unloaded, so the signal voltage swing becomes larger. Therefore the voltage gain increases.
